title: Trail and Compass
premise: Gideon Zhou, a mountain guide erased from two countries' registries after a disaster he may or may not have caused, is dragged back into the world when a government survey team vanishes on the Larkya Glacier, leaving intact gear and no footprints. Hired unofficially by the team's desperate cartographer, Gideon follows a trail that only he can read — because it was laid using his own old route codes. As monsoon floods strand them with a stranger named Asha whose memory of him doesn't match his own, Gideon must decide whether loyalty to a dead friend's reputation matters more than the truth of what happened three years ago. The story ends at the calving glacier: Gideon finds the survey team's survivor, exposes the falsified report that blacklisted him, and chooses to sign his real name to the rescue log — reclaiming identity over invisibility.
about_author: Yara Iversen is a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent six seasons in the Himalaya before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a farmhouse in western Norway, where she keeps her grandfather's brass compass on the desk as a reminder that every direction is a choice.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Three years into exile, Gideon guides trekkers under a borrowed name, measuring life in distances covered rather than time endured. A letter arrives offering cash for one off-book job: find a missing survey team. He refuses, then burns the refusal. Emotional beat: the ache of a man who has made peace with being no one.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Plea
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The sender turns out to be Mirela Osei, a government cartographer whose four-person survey team vanished near the Larkya Glacier. She shows him their last transmission — coordinates plotted in route codes only Gideon ever used. Emotional beat: recognition and dread; someone out there speaks his dead language.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At the abandoned high camp, Gideon finds tents pitched perfectly, food cached, radios functional — and not a single footprint in days-old snow. Mirela insists it's impossible; Gideon knows exactly what kind of person leaves no tracks. Emotional beat: cold fear sharpening into professional obsession.

chapters.title: Asha
chapters.summary: Asha's POV. A weathered woman appears on the moraine claiming to be a glaciologist studying calving seasons — but she greets Gideon by a name he buried years ago. She remembers a night in Kathmandu he has no memory of. Emotional beat: uncanny intimacy with a stranger who claims shared history.

chapters.title: Route Codes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Following coded cairns up the valley, Gideon admits the truth to Mirela: the codes are his own invention, taught to exactly one other person — Devi, his partner who died in the avalanche that ended his career. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as guilt; the past walking beside him.

chapters.title: Monsoon Breaks
chapters.summary: Asha's POV. The storm arrives early, trapping the trio below a swollen river. Asha reveals she has a leaking boat cached downstream and insists they take it, though the river runs toward restricted territory Gideon cannot enter. Emotional beat: forced trust; every choice costs something.

chapters.title: Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Bailing water through the night, Gideon tests Asha's story of Kathmandu and catches contradictions — yet her knowledge of his habits is unnervingly precise. Mirela suspects Asha is government surveillance. Emotional beat: paranoia fraying an already fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Restricted Water
chapters.summary: Asha's POV. They pass a checkpoint in fog; Asha talks them through with papers that shouldn't exist. Privately, she recalls the Kathmandu night from her side — a promise Gideon made while feverish, which he cannot remember making. Emotional beat: the loneliness of holding someone else's forgotten word.

chapters.title: What Devi Knew
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In a cave shelter, Gideon finally tells Mirela his version of the avalanche: Devi led the commercial group onto the glacier against warnings, and Gideon signed the report that blamed conditions instead of Devi — protecting a dead friend's name at the cost of his own career. Emotional beat: confession as relief and self-indictment.

chapters.title: The Second Set of Codes
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. Mirela decodes the cairn sequence and realizes it isn't leading to the missing team's camp — it's leading away from something, marking a hazard zone the official maps omit. Someone wanted this valley kept secret. Emotional beat: the dawning sense that the disappearance is deliberate.

chapters.title: Radio Ghost
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A broken transmission comes through: Devi's voice, or a recording of it, reciting coordinates. Gideon must confront the possibility Devi survived the avalanche — and never came looking for him. Emotional beat: hope weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Asha's Ledger
chapters.summary: Asha's POV. Caught copying Gideon's route notes, Asha confesses partially: she was hired to verify whether 'the guide who lied' was still alive, by people tied to the survey contract. But she kept working after the job ended, and won't say why. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with unexpected devotion.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The glacier begins to calve early — the brief window when the hidden route opens. Gideon calculates they have roughly forty hours before the ice wall seals the valley for another year. Emotional beat: urgency compressing every unresolved question into a deadline.

chapters.title: The Hazard Zone
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. Inside the marked zone, Mirela finds the survey team's data cache: evidence that the government knew the glacier was destabilizing and suppressed the report — the same style of falsification used against Gideon three years ago. Emotional beat: righteous fury; the pattern has a name.

chapters.title: Devi's Tent
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They find a living camp: Devi, half-blind and frost-scarred, surviving three years in the ice valley, laying codes no one was meant to follow. Devi didn't die in the avalanche — he fled the blame Gideon took for him. Emotional beat: shattered loyalty; the truth he protected was a lie he chose.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Devi begs Gideon to keep the secret again — the suppression, the survival, all of it — arguing the truth will destroy the families who mourned him. Gideon looks at Mirela, at the cache, at his own blacklisted name. Emotional beat: the book's thematic crux, held in silence.

chapters.title: The Ice Wall Closes
chapters.summary: Asha's POV. The calving accelerates; the exit route begins collapsing. Asha reveals her final secret: she is Devi's sister, who hired herself onto the search to learn if her brother lived — and she will not leave without him. Emotional beat: love as stubbornness against impossible odds.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes of Sky
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Climax part one: guiding four people across actively calving ice, Gideon uses the route codes as they were meant to be used — reading the mountain honestly. A serac fall cuts the party in two; Gideon goes back for Devi against all logic. Emotional beat: courage as fidelity to truth, not to lies.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Climax part two: Gideon reaches Devi, forces him to walk, and carries him through the collapsing route as the ice wall seals behind them. On the far side, Devi, broken open, agrees to testify. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured; the debt between them finally named.

chapters.title: Signing His Name
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. At base camp, Mirela drafts the true report — the suppressed hazard data, the falsified records, Devi alive. She asks Gideon how to list the rescuing guide. He gives his real name for the first time in three years. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, quietly, on paper.

chapters.title: Two Countries
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Aftermath: inquiries begin, bans are contested, and Gideon learns he can return to one of the countries that erased him. Devi faces consequences but also restitution; Asha stays to finish her sister-brother accounting. Emotional beat: justice as slow repair, not fireworks.

chapters.title: Compass North
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Epilogue: a season later, Gideon leads his first legal expedition, carrying a new compass alongside the old brass one Asha gave him. He measures life in years now, not miles. Final beat: the direction you face matters less than choosing it with your eyes open.
